arguments.value: This is a sponsored research and license agreement between ArTara, Inc. and The University of Iowa, with the University’s Principal Investigator, Richard Smith, M.D., identified in the agreement. It was signed effective November 28, 2018. The agreement covers a project in which the University and ArTara, with a CRO, use University clinical data from the OK-432 program to support development and regulatory filings for ArTara’s TARA-002 product for lymphangioma worldwide. The University grants ArTara an exclusive license to use the program data for the project and regulatory filings, and an exclusive right of reference to the University’s regulatory filings; the University may assign the IND to ArTara if requested. ArTara funds the project at $30,000 per year, may owe an FDA-approval milestone payment, royalty payments on net sales, and sales milestone payments. The University keeps ownership of the original program data and medical records, while ArTara owns project documentation it creates and each party owns or shares inventions according to who developed them. The agreement includes confidentiality, publication review, insurance, indemnification, and termination terms. ArTara may terminate on 30 days’ written notice, and either party may terminate the project on 30 days’ written notice; certain obligations survive termination. The governing law is the State of Iowa.
